wins.text: Net revenues of $14.6B in Q2, EPS of $10.91, ROE of 12.8% (14.8% for H1 2025)
Equities net revenues hit a record $4.3B, up significantly YoY; equities intermediation revenues of $2.6B rose 45% YoY
Advisory revenues of $1.2B rose 71% YoY; GS holds #1 M&A league table position with ~$85B lead in announced volume over nearest peer
Total financing revenues reached a record $2.8B, up 23% YoY — sixth consecutive quarterly record — now comprising over 1/3 of FICC and equities revenues

Assets under supervision rose to a record $3.3T; wealth management client assets hit a record $1.7T; 30th consecutive quarter of long-term fee-based net inflows; Board approved 33% dividend increase to $4/share

risks.text: Challenging harvesting environment for historical principal investments (~$8B remaining); modest net losses in private portfolio driven by real estate markdowns; H2 2025 equity/debt investment results expected to be more muted vs. medium-term run rate
Uncertainty persists in industries highly sensitive to trade policy; number of trade agreements yet to materialize; ultimate impact of higher tariffs on growth unknown
Stress Capital Buffer (SCB) transparency remains opaque — management cannot fully explain or guarantee durability of the improvement to 3.4% SCB; regulatory capital regime remains fluid
Geopolitical concerns have intensified in multiple regions, particularly the Middle East, creating potential for unexpected market disruptions
Debt underwriting revenues fell 5% YoY amid lower leveraged finance activity; commodities and mortgages were weak within FICC intermediation

guidance_items.detail: Medium-term ROE/ROTE target of mid-to-high teens reaffirmed with increased confidence given regulatory tailwinds and business mix improvement
CET1 operating buffer of 50-100 bps above regulatory minimum (10.9% as of Oct 1) reaffirmed as ongoing philosophy
Full-year effective tax rate expected at approximately 22%; YTD at 20.2%
Alternatives fundraising expected to be in line with recent years; incentive fees of $1B annual target expected to ramp more materially in 2026-2027
H2 2025 equity/debt investment revenues expected to be more muted relative to medium-term run rate due to challenging harvesting environment

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Durability and transparency of the SCB improvement — management did not proactively address whether the stress capital buffer gains are sustainable or model-driven
Tokenization and digital assets / stablecoin regulatory framework as a business opportunity — not mentioned in prepared remarks
Whether trading/markets revenue can remain robust if investment banking activity accelerates — potential cannibalization or moderation not addressed proactively
